q7.answer: Clients no longer copy the key at construction. On each provider call they call secrets.get(name) on the in-memory holder and build the Authorization header from it. The refresh thread swaps new values into the holder under a lock, so the next call uses the new key with no restart. The singletons stay, since they hold no key.

q8.answer: By hand, by the security on-call engineer. They list pods from the cluster, read each pod's latest refresh log line (version ids only) in the central logs, and compare it with the store's current version ids via the store CLI. They also check that no refresh alert is open and, where the provider shows last use, that the old key is unused. The result goes in the ticket and the on-call engineer signs off before revocation.

q9.answer: 1) Set store paths and access rules, and test them. 2) Issue new keys at providers (old stay active), test-call them, and write them to the store. 3) One PR: add the secrets module, switch clients to read from the store, remove api_key from the yaml, and add the CI guard. 4) Merge and rolling deploy. 5) Verify and soak. 6) Block old images and look for other users of the old keys. 7) Confirm every instance is on the new keys, then revoke the old keys. Rotation happens before the switch so both keys work during rollout, and revocation comes last.

q10.answer: With APP_ENV=local (make run), keys come from fixed fake keys in the local_secrets section of config/app.local.yaml, with base_urls pointing at local stubs. No credentials are used and there is no store call. Optionally make run-sandbox uses APP_ENV=dev and reads sandbox keys from orders-api/dev/* under the developer's own identity. Nobody reads prod secrets.

q11.answer: The attempt fails, because any failed read fails the whole attempt and the next attempt re-reads all three. A not-found is handled the same as any other failure. After the 4th failed attempt it logs the error without values and exits non-zero, and it never turns ready. During a rolling deploy this halts the rollout and the old pods keep serving.
